correction_2026-11-26_pm: supersedes the numbers first committed in 4ebb1b1: the initial version of this script computed anchors with date-minus-timedelta(hours) arithmetic, which drops sub-day offsets (8h anchor landed 16h AFTER the valid instant - look-ahead - and 32h at valid-24h). Anchors are now computed with explicit UTC datetimes: valid D 08:00 UTC minus lead, converted to the verified UTC-8 CSV clock. Model scores also shifted slightly because the common-date intersection changed with anchor availability.

anchor_availability.available_at_init: NO - the same-lead construction puts the anchor exactly AT the init instant (anchor = valid - lead = init), and an observation is not transmitted before it exists; observed NRCS archive latency: hourly >38h, daily SNOTEL <32h, COOP daily >35h
anchor_availability.why_symmetric_upper_bound: SYMMETRIC: anchor sits lead-hours before the valid instant, the same horizon the model covers. UPPER BOUND: zero-lag anchor is the best possible persistence estimate; a real-time anchor must sit earlier and cannot do better in expectation. The benchmark uses observations unavailable at issue time - it is retrospective.
anchor_availability.consequence: persistence wins DESPITE the favorable anchor, so 'models track quiet-window depth worse than persistence at these leads' is a conservative retrospective conclusion, not an operational one.

lead_8h.contrast_note: daily persistence is anchored on the prior daily actual (zero-lag); hourly persistence is anchored lead-hours before the valid instant - the honest same-lead benchmark
